subject: science
passage: Pacific salmon hatch in freshwater streams, then swim out to the ocean, where they spend several years feeding and growing. When they are ready to reproduce, most return to the very stream where they hatched, sometimes traveling hundreds of kilometers. Each stream carries a distinctive mix of chemicals from its soil and plants, and young salmon appear to memorize this scent before leaving. These observations suggest that adult salmon ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: rely mainly on their eyesight to recognize familiar landmarks.
choices.B: probably use smell to help them find their home streams.
choices.C: can reproduce only in the ocean, far from where they hatched.
choices.D: choose a new stream each year based on how much food it holds.

explanation.why: Each stream has its own scent, young salmon seem to memorize it, and adults return to the stream where they hatched. The most logical link is that the remembered scent helps guide them home.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text describes scent, not sight; eyesight is never mentioned.
explanation.B: Correct. A memorized stream scent is the only guide the text describes, so smell probably helps them return.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says salmon return to freshwater streams to reproduce, not that they reproduce in the ocean.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says most salmon return to the same stream where they hatched, not a new one.
